conventions: הַיּוֹם is aligned two ways in this chapter and neither is a split, because the ASV writes two different English expressions for it. At DEU.15.5 it writes *this day*: a determiner stands in the article's place, so the article takes *this* under rule 41 and יוֹם takes *day*. At DEU.15.15 it writes *to day*: one adverbial rendering of which no morpheme owns a part, so the article and the noun share one unit under rule 30, headed on יוֹם and on *day*, which is how the corpus reads all five of its הַ+יוֹם → *to day* units. Read which English the ASV wrote before choosing, and do not treat the pair as an inconsistency.

The dative לְ with a pronominal suffix is placed by what the ASV spends on the relation, not by the lemma or by the BSB comparison. Where the ASV writes a preposition it takes it — *unto him* at 15.8, 15.10 and 15.14 — and where the ASV writes a bare English indirect object, object or subject it is unrepresented under rule 40, the suffix taking the pronoun that realizes it: *give him*, *furnish him* against *giveth thee*, *promised thee*, *he wanteth*, *it is well with him*, *he shall be thy servant*. Both shapes occur within one verse at 15.10 and at 15.14. This division accounts for twelve of the chapter's thirty-three BSB disagreements and is a documented convention difference rather than an error.

The chapter's six preposition-plus-noun fusions divide rule 23 as follows and are consistent: where one morpheme carries content the other lacks, that morpheme heads — לִפְנֵי on פָּנֶה (15.20), מִקֶּרֶב on קֶרֶב (15.11), בִּגְלַל on גָּלָל (15.10), and the idiomatic בְעֵינֶיךָ → *unto* on עַיִן (15.18, under rule 40's closing paragraph, since the governed noun keeps no English of its own). Where neither does, the morpheme standing first heads — מֵעִם → *from* on מִן at 15.12, 15.13, 15.16 and 15.18, and likewise עַל־כֵּן on עַל (15.11, 15.15), כַּאֲשֶׁר on כְּ (15.6) and אֶפֶס כִּי on אֶפֶס (15.4).
report: Read all 47 candidate groups plus the full dump end to end. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed either by a difference in the ASV's own wording or by a morpheme actually standing in one context and not the other; no construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license it. patches is empty.

The groups worth naming: הַיּוֹם is split at 15.5 (*this day*, article takes *this* under rule 41) and fused at 15.15 (*to day*, one rendering under rule 30 headed on *day*, matching the corpus's five הַ+יוֹם → *to day* units) — two ASV renderings, not two analyses. The dative לְ takes *unto* where the ASV writes one (15.8, 15.10, 15.14) and is unrepresented where the ASV writes a bare English object or subject (15.4, 15.6, 15.7, 15.9, 15.10, 15.14, 15.16, 15.17), which is rule 40's condition read on the English rather than the lemma. אֵת is unrepresented by default and takes *of*/*Of* only in the two נָגַשׂ → *exact of* clauses (15.2, 15.3), one rule-16 family applied twice. אֶחָד → *one* / *any*, אֶבְיוֹן → *poor* / *a poor man* / *the poor*, כֹּל → *every* / *all* / *any … whatsoever* and לֹא → *not* / *no* / *never* / *nought* each follow the word the ASV wrote, with the determiner going to whichever morpheme licenses it (rules 15, 35, 41, 46).

Construct-chain articles are counted, not positioned, and the counts come out differently for good reason: 15.2 דְּבַר הַשְּׁמִטָּה → *the manner of the release* writes two *the*s, so nothing is fronted (rule 29's arthrous case), while 15.9 שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה → *the year of release* and שְׁנַת הַשֶּׁבַע → *The seventh year* each write one, which the rectum's article takes fronted. Agreement articles are uniformly unrepresented (15.5, 15.10, 15.12, 15.15, 15.19) under rule 47, and an article whose determiner slot a suffix or demonstrative pronoun already holds is uniformly unrepresented under rule 41's limit (15.5, 15.7, 15.9, 15.10, 15.15).

The table is blind to `added`, so I checked the five added units against the supplied words that were not marked added. The three supplied object *it*s (15.2, 15.3, 15.17) are consistent with each other and with the written object suffixes that take *it* elsewhere (rule 44). The supplied *as if* at 15.21 is rule 55's subordinator over a clause with no conjunction in it, while 15.10's *that thou puttest … unto* is rule 46's noun recast as a relative clause (the מִבְטַחַיִךְ shape) — different constructions, both notes naming the competing reading. The supplied *in* at 15.8 is the one place a supplied preposition was marked added rather than folded into a neighbouring unit; its note carries the alternative.

BSB: 33 disagreements, all convention differences — 14 articles, 12 recast prepositions, 3 object markers, one unrendered waw at 15.17 (the ASV writes no connective before *unto the door*), one ethical dative suffix at 15.9 (*Beware* alone). The only analytical one is 15.2 יָד + suffix inside בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה יָדוֹ → *creditor*: one English word for four morphemes forces something unrepresented, and rule 30 forbids absorbing a morpheme whose sense the word does not carry, so the hand phrase is left out. That is the chapter's closest call, it is defensible, its competing reading is already in the verse note, and I have not changed it. No genuine error found; nothing was altered to move the aggregate.

Promotions and amendments: none. Everything this chapter decided was already settled by rules 15, 23, 25, 29, 30, 34, 40, 41, 44, 46, 55 and 56, including the two verses carrying "Corrected" notes — 15.15's *to day* fusion is rule 30's one-rendering condition, and 15.22's twice-realized תֹּאכֲלֶנּוּ is the sentence rule 34 already has directing that the coordination be read for a verb the Hebrew writes once. A rule restating those would only crowd them.
